title: aon_timer: wake-up timer and watchdog register facts (control case)
conditions: Programming the wake-up timer and the watchdog as the README, the theory of operation and the programmer's guide describe.
C1 records a width in bits; the other settings are encoded as 1 if the statement about the design holds and 0 if it does not.

requirements.text: The number of cycles per tick is one more than the 12-bit [`WKUP_CTRL.prescaler`](doc/registers.md#wkup_ctrl) field.
The wakeup signal (`wkup_req_o`) stays high until software explicitly acknowledges it by software writing 0 to [`WKUP_CAUSE`](doc/registers.md#wkup_cause).
requirements.note: Line 75 says the same for a watchdog bark.

requirements.text: To clear the level interrupt (`intr_wkup_timer_expired_o`), write 1 to the field [`INTR_STATE.wkup_timer_expired`](doc/registers.md#intr_state).
requirements.note: Line 77 says the same for the watchdog bark interrupt.
Where the 64-bit wake-up count and threshold are held.
The link text says WKUP_THOLD_HI; the link goes to WKUP_THOLD_LO.

requirements.text: 5. If desired, lock the watchdog configuration by writing 0 to the `regwen` bit in [`WDOG_REGWEN`](registers.md#wdog_regwen).

design.note: The wake-up request output is WKUP_CAUSE itself, so clearing it drops the request.
The core forms the 64-bit threshold with WKUP_THOLD_HI as the upper half.
Bits 31:0 are held by WKUP_THOLD_LO, not WKUP_THOLD_HI.
The same line as D6: WKUP_THOLD_LO is the lower half, so WKUP_THOLD_HI does not hold bits 31:0.
WDOG_CTRL is locked by WDOG_REGWEN, as are WDOG_BARK_THOLD and WDOG_BITE_THOLD (lines 286 and 299).

claims.setting: writing 0 to WKUP_CAUSE clears the wake-up request (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

claims.setting: writing 1 to an INTR_STATE field clears the interrupt (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

claims.setting: WKUP_THOLD_HI holds bits 63:32 of the threshold (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

claims.setting: WKUP_THOLD_HI holds bits 31:0 of the threshold (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: disagrees

claims.setting: writing 0 to WDOG_REGWEN locks the watchdog configuration (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

generated_from_same_input: D1, D2, D4, D5, D7, D9 and D10 are in aon_timer.hjson, from which reggen generates the register RTL and registers.md; those generated files are not counted as further evidence. D3, D6 and D8 are in the hand-written RTL (D6 and D8 are the same line). R1 to R6 are hand-written.
finding: Five of the six statements agree with the design. R5's link text names WKUP_THOLD_HI for bits 31:0, which WKUP_THOLD_LO holds; the link itself goes to WKUP_THOLD_LO. The register tests in csr/ also observed C6 in simulation: once WDOG_REGWEN is cleared, WDOG_CTRL, WDOG_BARK_THOLD and WDOG_BITE_THOLD ignore writes.
missing_information: This case reads the register description and the RTL. The register tests in csr/ simulate the lock (C6) but are not part of this case's evidence.
ambiguities: R5's link goes to the right register, so a reader who follows the link finds WKUP_THOLD_LO; a reader who reads the text does not.
out_of_scope: What the prescaler and thresholds do over time (the timer's counting), which is not checked here.
